paper_id: Integrating Tree Path in Transformer for Code Representation
title: Integrating Tree Path in Transformer for Code Representation
motivation: Sequential models struggle to capture code structure; Transformers lack structural inductive bias; GNNs have local representations
problem_framing: Integrate AST path encodings (relative and absolute) into Transformer attention module to capture code syntax and semantics
key_insight: Relative paths reveal token relationships (patterns like for-loops); absolute paths reveal per-token program behavior; both can bias self-attention
method_signature: TPTrans: modify Transformer attention with path-encoded relative position representations and layer-normalized GRU encoders
evaluation_criteria: Code summarization F1/precision/recall on Python, Ruby, JavaScript, Go (CSN dataset)
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: TPTrans-α (with absolute path) shows almost no gain over TPTrans alone; path overlap exists between absolute and relative paths
evidence_for_taste: struggle to capture the structural complexity
representation of GNNs tends to be local
lacks the ability to model the structural complexity
the gain from absolute path encoding is almost weak
thinking_moves: 把positional encoding的类比嫁接到AST path encoding
分离相对路径和绝对路径的信息贡献
通过消融实验逐步去除路径编码的子模块
用路径退化实验验证'路径vs距离'的信息量差异
发现语言间路径长度分布差异导致的性能异常
extraction_notes: Year and venue not explicitly stated in paper. Abstract mentions CodeSearchNet dataset but no specific conference publication. The paper appears to be from arXiv based on reference style, likely a conference submission.
